conditions.name: Acute appendicitis
conditions.opd: Suspect with migratory periumbilical-to-right-lower-quadrant pain, anorexia, nausea and localized tenderness. Presentation may be atypical in pregnancy, older adults and children. Assess vitals, peritonism and pregnancy differential; obtain CBC/CRP, urinalysis and pregnancy test when relevant. Imaging follows local pathway; ultrasound is often used first in children/pregnancy and CT may be appropriate in non-pregnant adults when uncertain.
conditions.indoor: Suspected appendicitis needs timely surgical assessment. Keep nil by mouth if likely to need surgery; provide analgesia and fluids as indicated. In hospital, arrange surgical review, imaging and peri-operative antibiotics per local protocol. Appendectomy is standard for many patients; selected uncomplicated cases may discuss antibiotics-only management with a surgeon. Discharge only after definitive plan, stable observations, oral intake and clear return precautions.

conditions.name: Acute cholecystitis
conditions.opd: Persistent right-upper-quadrant pain, fever and Murphy sign may suggest acute cholecystitis, commonly due to gallstones. Check CBC, CRP, liver profile, renal function and lipase; ultrasound is first-line. Consider MRCP when common bile duct stones are suspected.
conditions.indoor: Suspected acute cholecystitis generally needs same-day hospital/surgical assessment. In hospital provide fluids if indicated, analgesia and antiemetic; antibiotics when indicated and early laparoscopic cholecystectomy when feasible. Severe/unfit patients may need specialist-guided drainage or alternative management. Discharge only with a clear definitive plan and return precautions.

conditions.name: Acute pancreatitis
conditions.opd: Acute persistent epigastric pain often radiating to the back with nausea/vomiting. Diagnosis generally requires 2 of 3: typical pain, lipase/amylase greater than 3 times upper limit, or characteristic imaging. Check lipase, CBC, electrolytes/renal function, glucose, liver profile, calcium and triglycerides when relevant; ultrasound assesses gallstones.
conditions.indoor: Suspected acute pancreatitis requires hospital assessment. Use reassessed isotonic crystalloid fluids tailored to status, adequate analgesia and early oral/enteral feeding as tolerated. Treat the cause. Antibiotics are not routine for sterile pancreatitis. Urgent ERCP is reserved for selected biliary obstruction/cholangitis scenarios. Discharge when pain is controlled, oral intake tolerated, observations stable and cause/follow-up plan established.

conditions.name: Small bowel obstruction
conditions.opd: Colicky abdominal pain, distension, vomiting and failure to pass stool/flatus. Prior abdominal surgery is a common risk factor; consider hernia and malignancy. Assess hernial orifices; obtain CBC, electrolytes, renal function and lactate if ischaemia is suspected. CT abdomen/pelvis usually helps define cause and complications.
conditions.indoor: Suspected obstruction needs urgent ED/surgical referral, not routine outpatient constipation care. In hospital: nil by mouth, IV fluids/electrolyte correction, nasogastric decompression when indicated, urine-output monitoring and early surgical review. Peritonitis, strangulation, ischaemia or deterioration requires urgent operation. Discharge only after resolution and treating-team confirmation of safe intake and follow-up.

conditions.name: Perforated peptic ulcer
conditions.opd: Sudden severe abdominal pain, guarding/rigidity and peritonitis; presentation may be atypical in older or immunocompromised patients. This is a surgical emergency. Obtain CBC, electrolytes/renal function, lactate and group/crossmatch; CT if stable and available, but do not delay resuscitation or surgery in an unstable patient.
conditions.indoor: Immediate emergency transfer and surgical consultation; keep nil by mouth. In hospital, resuscitate, give IV fluids/blood if indicated, broad-spectrum IV antibiotics, IV PPI and analgesia, with urgent surgical source control. Test/treat H. pylori after stabilization as appropriate. Discharge after definitive treatment and clinical recovery with ulcer-cause and follow-up plans.

conditions.name: Upper GI bleeding
conditions.opd: Haematemesis, coffee-ground vomiting or melaena. Assess for shock and consider variceal bleeding in chronic liver disease. Investigations: CBC, urea/creatinine, electrolytes, liver profile, coagulation, group/crossmatch; ECG/troponin when indicated. Risk-stratify and arrange endoscopy after resuscitation.
conditions.indoor: Active bleeding, syncope, hypotension, tachycardia or haematemesis needs emergency care. Resuscitate first and protect airway when needed. Endoscopy is generally performed within 24 hours after stabilization; suspected variceal bleeding requires prompt specialist pathway. Discharge after source treatment, no ongoing bleeding, stable observations and a clear medicine/follow-up plan.

conditions.name: Acute urinary retention
conditions.opd: Inability to pass urine with painful distended bladder; causes include prostatic obstruction, medicines, urethral stricture, neurological disease and infection. Assess abdomen/genitalia and focused neurology; bladder scan, urinalysis and renal function as appropriate. New saddle anaesthesia or leg weakness is a red flag.
conditions.indoor: Acute retention usually needs urgent assessment and bladder decompression by trained staff unless urethral injury is suspected. Monitor drained volume, haematuria and post-obstructive diuresis when relevant; arrange trial without catheter/urology follow-up. Suspected cauda equina, sepsis, trauma or failed catheterization requires emergency escalation. Discharge only with a safe catheter-care plan and review date.

conditions.name: Renal colic / suspected ureteric stone
conditions.opd: Severe flank pain radiating to groin, often with nausea and haematuria. Fever/sepsis with obstruction is a urological emergency. Check urinalysis, renal function and pregnancy test when relevant; imaging follows local pathway (ultrasound in pregnancy; low-dose non-contrast CT commonly in non-pregnant adults).
conditions.indoor: Urgent ED referral for fever/rigors, anuria, solitary kidney, pregnancy with severe symptoms, uncontrolled pain/vomiting or renal impairment. Analgesia, antiemetic and fluids to correct deficit; avoid forced hydration. Evaluate stone size/location and need for urological intervention. Discharge only if pain controlled, no infection/AKI/high-risk feature and follow-up arranged.

conditions.name: Cellulitis and skin abscess
conditions.opd: Cellulitis causes spreading erythema, warmth, swelling and tenderness. A fluctuant abscess generally needs drainage. Rapid progression, pain out of proportion or systemic toxicity may indicate necrotizing infection. Tests/cultures are reserved for severity, systemic illness, unusual exposure or deep infection.
conditions.indoor: Mild uncomplicated cellulitis may be treated outpatient if stable and follow-up is reliable. Admit/escalate for sepsis, rapid progression, high-risk sites, immunocompromise or suspected deep/necrotizing infection. Incision and drainage is primary treatment for a drainable abscess; antibiotics depend on systemic features, surrounding cellulitis, host factors and local resistance. Review if not improving within 48–72 hours.

conditions.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
conditions.opd: Hyperglycaemia or known diabetes with ketonaemia and metabolic acidosis; euglycaemic DKA can occur, including with SGLT2 inhibitors. Check bedside glucose and blood ketones, venous blood gas, electrolytes, renal function and ECG; investigate precipitant such as infection, missed insulin, MI, pregnancy or medicines.
conditions.indoor: Suspected DKA requires emergency hospital transfer, not home/outpatient management. Use a current monitored institutional protocol for fluids, IV insulin when indicated, potassium-guided replacement and frequent glucose/ketone/electrolyte checks. Check potassium before insulin and replace according to protocol; treat precipitant. Discharge only after biochemical resolution, safe transition to subcutaneous insulin, education, supplies and follow-up.
